radiology_notes.text:
CT CHEST WITHOUT CONTRAST, ___

COMPARISON:  MRCP from ___ and outside CT abdomen of ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Volumetric, multidetector CT of the chest was performed without
intravenous or oral contrast.  Images are presented for display in the axial
plane at 5-mm and 1-mm collimation.  A series of multiplanar reformation
images were also submitted for review.

FINDINGS:  Small calcified lymph nodes are present in the right paratracheal
and right hilar nodal stations, along with a large calcified right upper lobe
granuloma, consistent with previous granulomatous exposure.  Heart size is
normal, and there is no pericardial or pleural effusion.

Nonspecific biapical scarring is incidentally noted, as well as linear foci of
scarring or atelectasis at the lung bases.  A dependent triangular opacity in
left lower lobe posteriorly (166, 5) measuring 3 mm in diameter is probably
due to a small focal area of dependent atelectasis, particularly considering
characteristic findings of dependent atelectasis in both lower lobes at this
level.  A linearly oriented focal opacity in the right middle lobe anteriorly
(198, 5) is unchanged from the prior study and attributed to localized
scarring.  A 3 mm diameter peribronchial nodule in the right upper lobe
anteriorly (116, 5) cannot be assessed for retrospective stability as to
previous CT abdomen did not extend to this level.

There are no suspicious focal skeletal abnormalities.

The exam was not specifically tailored to evaluate the subdiaphragmatic
region, but hepatic ductal dilation, left hepatic lobe atrophy, common hepatic
duct hilar mass, attenuated left portal vein, mildly enlarged abdominal lymph
nodes and mild splenomegaly have been more fully evaluated on recent MRCP of
the abdomen.  Bile duct stent has been placed, and likely explains the
presence of pneumobilia.  Oral contrast is present within the gallbladder.

IMPRESSION:
1.  3 mm noncalcified right upper lobe lung nodule is potentially a benign
finding, but followup CT in three to six months is suggested given history of
cholangiocarcinoma in order to exclude a small focus of metastatic disease.

2.  Please see report of recent MRCP of ___ for complete
description of subdiaphragmatic findings.
